writeup: TIC 257806221 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 19.924111 days, identified through automated analysis of TESS photometry data. The primary eclipse produces a 5.25 percent dimming of the star's light, while no secondary eclipse was detected. Pixel-level difference imaging confirms the eclipse signal originates from the target location, though with a centroid offset of 7.3 arcseconds. A notable open question exists: the alternating eclipses show significantly different depths, which may indicate the true period is double what initial analysis suggested. The star does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a previously unreported target. With a detection significance of 161.7 in the box-least-squares search and a machine-learning screening score of 0.56, this candidate merits further investigation to clarify its orbital properties.
